B1.2 Computational Thinking

Turn complexity into solvable structure

The app keeps failing. The code is not the first problem.

A transport app now handles sign-up, route planning, payment, and safeguarding in one tangled system.

Where do we simplify first?

Two moves, two purposes

Move What it does
Abstraction Keeps essentials (capacity, timing, stop order) and removes irrelevant detail.
Decomposition Splits one large problem into smaller sub-problems with clearer ownership.

Abstraction decides what matters. Decomposition decides where the work splits.

Try it on a clinic booking system

Identify:

  • Two details to remove through abstraction
  • Three sub-problems to create through decomposition

Then: abstraction/decomposition worksheet in Activities.

You solved one case. Can you reuse that thinking?

Pattern recognition finds repeated structure.

Algorithmic thinking turns that structure into an ordered, finite process.

Where pattern recognition meets algorithmic thinking

Scenario: school markbook processing for multiple classes.

  • Pattern recognition: each class repeats validation, threshold checks, and report formatting.
  • Algorithmic thinking: define exact steps for import, validate, calculate, and output.

The pattern gives reuse. The algorithm gives precision.

Now transfer the same logic

Apply both ideas to one domain:

  • machine learning
  • network monitoring
  • online retail search

State the repeated pattern, then write the algorithmic sequence that uses it.

Same four tools. Different domains.

Can abstraction, decomposition, pattern recognition, and algorithmic thinking explain decisions in software, networks, databases, and machine learning?

Domain lens challenge

Domain Likely first lens What it changes
Software systems Decomposition Modular teams and cleaner responsibilities
Machine learning Pattern recognition Signal detection in training data
Networks Abstraction Reasoning with layer models instead of raw packet detail
Databases Algorithmic thinking Explicit query and indexing logic

Pick one row and argue for a different first lens.

Then: domain-transfer worksheet in Activities.

If one of the four disappeared, which system would break first?

Choose software, machine learning, networks, or databases.

Defend the failure path with concrete reasoning.
